draft.title: Describing an association
card: Positive: as one variable increases, the other tends to increase. Negative: as one increases, the other tends to decrease. No direction: no clear trend.
Linear if the points follow a straight line pattern. Non-linear if they follow a curve.
Strong if the points sit close to a clear pattern. Weak if they are widely scattered around it. Moderate sits in between.
A strong association does not prove that one variable causes the other. Both may be affected by a third variable, or the link may be coincidence.
draft.remember: Describe direction, form and strength. A strong association does not prove cause.

a.q: A scatterplot has points that fall from left to right and sit close to a straight line. Which description fits best?
a.why: Points sloping down show a negative direction. A straight line pattern is linear, and points close to the line make it strong. Positive is wrong because the other variable decreases as the first increases.
a.clue: Read the points from left to right: do they rise or fall?

b.q: In Perth, daily ice cream sales and daily sunburn cases have a strong positive linear association. What does this association show?
opts: Neither variable is shown to cause the other
Ice cream sales are shown to cause sunburn cases
Sunburn cases are shown to cause ice cream sales
The association is weak, as neither causes the other
b.why: A strong association does not prove cause. A third variable, such as hot sunny weather, may affect both. Saying ice cream sales cause sunburn is tempting, but strength only describes how close the points sit to the pattern.
b.clue: Think about what else could affect both variables on a hot day.

b.best: Neither variable is shown to cause the other
